summary: The AI project cycle is a six-stage framework for developing AI solutions. The stages are problem scoping, data acquisition, data exploration, modeling, evaluation, and deployment. Problem scoping defines the problem using the four Ws: Who, What, Where, and Why. Data acquisition involves collecting relevant data. Data exploration uses visualization to discover patterns. Modeling uses machine learning techniques such as supervised and unsupervised learning. Evaluation measures how well the model performs. Deployment puts the completed AI solution into the real world.
questions: What are the six stages of the AI project cycle?
What are the four Ws used during problem scoping?
What is the purpose of data exploration?
What is the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?
answers: The six stages are problem scoping, data acquisition, data exploration, modeling, evaluation, and deployment.
Problem scoping is important because it clearly defines the problem and what the AI project is trying to accomplish.
The four Ws are Who, What, Where, and Why.
Data acquisition involves collecting the data needed for the AI project.
Data exploration helps people understand the data and identify patterns using techniques such as visualization.
Supervised learning uses labeled data, while unsupervised learning uses unlabeled data to find patterns.
A model is evaluated to determine how accurately and effectively it performs its intended task.
Deployment puts the completed AI solution into the real world so people can use it.
